title: Panova's restricted #P conjecture for Kronecker coefficients
statement:
Let $\textsf{ComputeKron}$ be the problem of computing $g(\lambda,\mu,\nu)$ from partitions $\lambda,\mu,\nu$. Write $\ell(\lambda)$ for the number of parts of $\lambda$, and let $(n^d)$ denote the rectangular partition with $d$ parts equal to $n$.

**Panova's restricted-case conjecture.** The following two statements are each equivalent to the unrestricted assertion that $\textsf{ComputeKron}$ is in $\#\mathrm{P}$:

$$
\textsf{ComputeKron}\in\#\mathrm{P}\text{ when }\ell(\lambda)=2
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\textsf{ComputeKron}\in\#\mathrm{P},
$$

and

$$
\textsf{ComputeKron}\in\#\mathrm{P}\text{ for }\mu=\nu=(n^d),\ \lambda\vdash nd
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\textsf{ComputeKron}\in\#\mathrm{P}.
$$

These equivalences identify two restricted families whose membership in $\#\mathrm{P}$ would already settle the general counting question. The surrounding text presents this as a conjectural complexity statement about Kronecker coefficients.
source_name: Greta Panova, “Complexity and asymptotics of structure constants”, arXiv:2305.02553 (2023).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.02553

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of May 2023).
